title: 3.4.21 Lab: Parameters, Return Values, and Arrow Syntax
description: Group code into reusable logic blocks with parameters and return values.

steps.title: Declare a function
steps.instructions: Create a function called `greet` that takes a name parameter and returns a greeting string.

requirements.title: greet function
requirements.description: Declare a function called greet. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: A function declaration starts with the word function, then the name greet, then parentheses and a body in braces.

requirements.title: Return value
requirements.hint: A function can hand a value back. Use the return keyword followed by the value you want to give back.

requirements.title: Arrow function
requirements.description: Write an arrow function. Help: 3.4.6 (Arrow Functions)
requirements.hint: An arrow function is written with =>. Put the parameters before the arrow and the body after it.

requirements.title: Call greet
requirements.description: Call the greet function. Help: 3.1.11 (The Function-Call Shape)
requirements.hint: Defining a function does nothing until you call it. Write its name followed by parentheses.

requirements.title: Multiple functions
requirements.description: Define at least 2 functions. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: Write two separate function definitions, not one. Give each its own name and body.
